<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919159_theRebbe_441" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919159_theRebbe_441__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions how Dovid's Torah study as "songs" could be contrary to the true intent, and explains through the concept of "Hashem is One" that unity includes the world, leading to the revelation of Atzmus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one must understand:</t>
    <t s="1">Behold, the engagement in Torah of Dovid in the manner of "Your statutes were songs for me" is in the aspect of Torah as it is from the aspect of the ratzon (will) of the Selfhood (Atzmi)</t>
    <t s="2">(as explained above at length),</t>
    <t s="3">and how is it possible that this should be not in accordance with the true intention?</t>
    <t s="4">And one can say the explanation in this:</t>
    <t s="5">According to what is said in the maamar at its beginning regarding the matter of "Hashem is One" (Hashem Echad),</t>
    <t s="6">that the explanation of "Echad" (One) is "Yachid" (Unique/Singular),</t>
    <t s="7">and why we say "Echad" and not "Yachid" is to teach that "Hashem and Elokim are entirely One."</t>
    <t s="8">And the matter is:</t>
    <t s="9">That the true concept of the unity of Hashem is that the unity is also from the perspective of the world.</t>
    <t s="10">And this is what is written "Hashem is One" (Hashem Echad),</t>
    <t s="11">for if it were written "Hashem is Yachid" (Unique),</t>
    <t s="12">the explanation would be that His unity, blessed be He, is from the perspective of Ein Sof</t>
    <t s="13">(and not from the perspective of the world),</t>
    <t s="14">and in order to emphasize that His unity, blessed be He, is also from the perspective of the world,</t>
    <t s="15">and even from the perspective of the world as it was created from the Name Elokim, which conceals and hides the Name Hashem,</t>
    <t s="16">therefore it is said</t>
    <t s="17">"Hashem is One" (Hashem Echad),</t>
    <t s="18">that even the Chet and Dalet (of Echad), which are the seven firmaments and earth and the four directions of the world,</t>
    <t s="19">are nullified to the Alef, the Yachid (Unique One) of the world.</t>
    <t s="20">For since "Hashem and Elokim are entirely One,"</t>
    <t s="21">behold, the Name Elokim does not truly conceal,</t>
    <t s="22">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="23">also the world, which came into being from the Name Elokim, is truly nullified, and "there is nothing besides Him."</t>
    <t s="24">And this extends to the nullification in the level and manner of "Yachid" (Unique) which is above "Echad" (One).</t>
    <t s="25">And through the unification of the two matters</t>
    <t s="26">(that His unity, blessed be He, is in the manner of Yachid,</t>
    <t s="27">and that this matter is also from the perspective of the world),</t>
    <t s="28">through this there is a revelation of the power of Atzmus (Essence) which includes and connects the matter of Echad and Yachid.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the Name Hashem contains three meanings—bringing into being, past-present-future, and the Essential Name—and their unity reveals the Essential Name, especially through the aspect of "bringing into being."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(i)</t>
    <t s="1">(b)</t>
    <t s="2">And one may add:</t>
    <t s="3">That the Name Hashem</t>
    <t s="4">("Hashem is One")</t>
    <t s="5">indicates all three matters</t>
    <t s="6">(Echad, Yachid, and the power of Atzmus that connects them).</t>
    <t s="7">For in Hashem there are three matters: a) Hashem from the term "Mahaveh" (He brings into being),</t>
    <t s="8">that this explanation of the Name Hashem indicates His connection to the worlds,</t>
    <t s="9">b) Hashem from the term "Hayah, Hoveh, v'Yihyeh" (He was, is, and will be),</t>
    <t s="10">that this explanation of the Name Hashem indicates that He is above the worlds,</t>
    <t s="11">and the third matter in the Name Hashem is that Hashem is the Essential Name (Shem HaEtzem),</t>
    <t s="12">meaning that it indicates His very Essence (Atzmuso), blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="13">For although in the Pardes</t>
    <t s="14">it is written that this—that the Name Hashem is the Essential Name—is only regarding the essence of the Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="15">meaning the lights that are invested in the vessels,</t>
    <t s="16">nevertheless, the conclusion of Chassidus</t>
    <t s="17">is that the explanation of "Essential Name" is regarding the Atzmus (Essence).</t>
    <t s="18">And behold, since all three matters are in that same Name,</t>
    <t s="19">it is therefore understood</t>
    <t s="20">that they are related to each other.</t>
    <t s="21">And this means that the unification of the two explanations in Hashem—</t>
    <t s="22">Hashem from the term "Mahaveh" and Hashem from the term "Hayah, Hoveh, v'Yihyeh" as one—</t>
    <t s="23">is from the aspect that Hashem is the Essential Name.</t>
    <t s="24">And it follows,</t>
    <t s="25">that through the fact that Hashem, who is above the worlds</t>
    <t s="26">(Hayah, Hoveh, v'Yihyeh as one)</t>
    <t s="27">is drawn down into Hashem from the term "Mahaveh,"</t>
    <t s="28">even though externally this is a matter of descent,</t>
    <t s="29">nevertheless, specifically through this the Essential Name within Him is revealed.</t>
    <t s="30">And moreover, the revelation of the Essential Name of Hashem is primarily in Hashem from the term "Mahaveh."</t>
    <t s="31">And as explained in many places,</t>
    <t s="32">that the reason the Name Hashem is the Essential Name, which indicates the Atzmus (Essence), is because the bringing into being of yesh mei'ayin (existence from nothing) is specifically through the power of Atzmus, whose existence is from its very Self.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the Rambam's three foundational principles correspond to the three aspects of the Name Hashem, with the third principle referring to Atzmus as the source of creation ex nihilo.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(i)</t>
    <t s="1">(c)</t>
    <t s="2">And based on this, one can also understand what the Rambam said</t>
    <t s="3">(cited in the aforementioned maamar at its beginning):</t>
    <t s="4">"The foundation of foundations and the pillar of wisdoms is to know that there is a First Existent, and He brings into existence all existence,</t>
    <t s="5">and all existences, from the heavens and the earth and what is between them, did not exist except from the truth of His existence."</t>
    <t s="6">For the mitzvah of knowledge is in three matters:</t>
    <t s="7">That there is a First Existent,</t>
    <t s="8">that He brings into existence all existence,</t>
    <t s="9">and that all existences, etc., did not exist except from the truth of His existence.</t>
    <t s="10">For these three matters correspond to the three matters mentioned above in Hashem.</t>
    <t s="11">"The foundation of foundations and the pillar of wisdoms" has the initial letters of Hashem.</t>
    <t s="12">"First Existent" means that He is prior to all,</t>
    <t s="13">above creation.</t>
    <t s="14">"He brings into existence all existence" is Hashem from the term "Mahaveh."</t>
    <t s="15">And "all existences, etc., did not exist except from the truth of His existence"—</t>
    <t s="16">"the truth of His existence" is the Atzmus (Essence) whose existence is from its very Self,</t>
    <t s="17">for the bringing into being of existences yesh mei'ayin (existence from nothing) is through the power of Atzmus</t>
    <t s="18">(as above),</t>
    <t s="19">the matter of the Essential Name.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
